roster.title: Roster
roster.subtitle: Build the monthly shift roster — pick a month, then assign shifts across your team.
roster.noCompanies: No companies in your scope to roster.
roster.shiftHint: A shift ending at or before its start crosses midnight (⊕). The schedule drives attendance OT; no roster falls back to the company policy.
roster.varianceHint: Rostered shifts that didn't go to plan — no-shows, late starts, short hours, or rest days worked.
roster.noEmployees: No active employees in this company.
roster.createShiftFirst: Create a shift above to start rostering.
roster.noRestWarningHint: Seven days in a row with a shift and no rest day — EA 1955 s.59 requires one rest day per week.
roster.bankInLieuConsentPrompt: This employee is within the First Schedule (statutory overtime pay applies). Banking time in lieu instead of the statutory cash premium needs the employee's explicit prior agreement. Confirm consent to proceed?
roster.multiBreakStorageHint: Multiple break windows are saved and shown, but the hours deducted still use their combined total — per-break precision is a future enhancement.
roster.generated: Roster generated for {employees} employees — {working} working-day and {rest} rest-day entries.
roster.generateHint: Fills every date in the range from the shift's weekly pattern: shift entries on working days and explicit rest days on the rest, so the company policy never silently overrides the pattern. Re-running overwrites the same dates.
roster.manageShiftsHint: Shift schedules are managed in Shift settings; a person's usual shift is set on their profile as their Default shift. Use the roster for date-specific exceptions.
roster.copyHint: Copies every shift and rest day from the source dates onto the target, keeping each day's position. Re-running overwrites the same target dates.
roster.copiedDone: Copied {rows} roster entries onto the target dates.
roster.copiedEmpty: No roster entries found in the source dates to copy.
roster.ghostHint: Grey = the employee's usual shift filling a date nothing was rostered on.

roster.templateNoteBlank: Leave a cell blank to keep that date exactly as it is.
roster.templateNoteCode: Type a shift code to roster that shift on that date.
roster.templateNoteRd: Type RD for a rostered rest day.
roster.templateNoteOff: Type OFF to remove any entry for that date.
roster.templateNoteMonth: Only dates inside {month} are saved — any other date column is reported and ignored.
roster.templateFailed: Could not build the template file.
roster.viewOnly: A supervisor views the roster; an HR Administrator changes it.

roster.rowConfirm: Set {count, plural, =1 {# date} other {# dates}} for this employee?

roster.applyRow: Apply to {count, plural, =1 {# date} other {# dates}}

roster.totalNormalHoursNormalHint: Worked out from your times and breaks. Change it if a normal day on this shift is a different length.
roster.totalNormalHoursSemiHint: Required on a Semi Flexi shift. Overtime starts once this many hours of work have been done, breaks not counted.
roster.breakFixedHint: Fixed means the break is taken at that clock time. Untick it and the employee takes the break whenever they like.
roster.breakFixedLockedHint: Every break on this shift is flexible, so Fixed cannot be ticked: the break is an allowance the employee may take at any time, not a clock time to be kept.
roster.dailyCutoffHint: Any clocking after this time counts towards the next day. Leave it off and the system keeps deciding that on its own, as it does today.
roster.halfDayCutoffHint: Clock out before this time and the day is treated as a half day.
roster.halfDayCutoffDerived: Worked out for you — half of {total} is {half} of work, breaks not counted (about {at}).
roster.halfDayCutoffDerivedPending: Worked out for you once the total normal working hours are set.
roster.dayKindHint: Full is an ordinary working day. Half is a working day with half the normal hours. Rest is the statutory rest day. Off is a non-working day that is not the rest day.
roster.flexibleBreakUse: Let employees take their break at any time
roster.flexibleBreakHint: With this on, the allowed minutes come off every worked day whether or not the employee took the break inside the times above — those times stay as guidance. It changes how hours are counted for this shift, so it is off until you turn it on.
roster.breakDeductionSummary: {deducted} comes off a full day, leaving {net} of normal working time.
roster.breakDeductionSemiHint: On a Semi Flexi shift the normal working time is the figure set above, not the window, so no total is worked out here.
roster.moreSettingsHint: Description, category, day type, earliest clock-in, latest clock-out, 2nd half-day clock-in, full-day leave, full-day overtime, normal-hours rounding, the overtime schedule and the shift premium — all still saved, all still editable.

list.provisionalEndHint: Probation end for full-time (defaults to +3 months); contract or internship end otherwise. Leave blank for none.
list.orgLabelsEmptyForCompany: No organization labels are configured for the selected company.

detail.maritalPcbNote: Marital status here drives leave eligibility only. Update the PCB/tax category separately if it also changes.
detail.taxNumberSharedTitle: {count, plural, one {This income tax reference number is already filed against another employee: {names}. Correct whichever record is wrong before you file — the CP39 prints what is stored under each employee.} other {This income tax reference number is already filed against other employees: {names}. detail.socsoCategoryHint: Auto follows PERKESO rules from the employee's age and citizenship. Pick a specific category to override, or No contribution to exempt SOCSO.
detail.eisCategoryHint: Auto follows PERKESO rules. Choose No contribution to exempt EIS.
detail.subjectToSkbbkHint: SKBBK (Lindung 24 Jam) — the self-employment injury scheme leg added on top of SOCSO.
detail.employerBearsHint: The contribution is still made and reported in full; the employee's share is funded by the employer instead of deducted from net pay.
detail.employerBearsEpfHint: When ticked, the employee's EPF contribution is still computed and reported in full, but the employer funds it instead of deducting it from net pay.
detail.tp3SectionTitle: Previous employment this year (TP3 / opening balances)
detail.tp3SectionDescription: From the employee’s Form TP3 (or pre-migration payroll): seeds the PCB accumulators when the year matches the pay period. Never shown on payslips or the EA.
detail.zakatSummaryDescription: Read-only summary of the current zakat election. Manage it in Payroll → Transaction Entry → Zakat.
detail.zakatSummaryInactive: No active zakat election for this employee.
detail.othersStatutoryHint: Statutory settings that do not belong under EPF, SOCSO, EIS or Tax Information.
detail.subjectToHrdfHint: When checked, this employee's qualifying earnings are included in the HRD Corp (HRDF) levy calculation during payroll; when unchecked, the employee is excluded entirely.
detail.subjectToHrdfFollowingDefault: Following the company's HRDF registration default. Save to set an explicit choice for this employee.
detail.subjectToHrdfCompanyNotRegistered: Set to Yes, but this employee’s company has no HRDF Contribution Rate (Organization ▸ Statutory), so payroll charges no levy for them. The choice is saved and takes effect once the company is registered.
detail.subjectToHrdfCompanyUnregisteredNote: This company has no HRDF Contribution Rate (Organization ▸ Statutory), so choosing Yes here is saved but charges no levy until the company is registered.
detail.dataPrivacyNote: Run a retention-guarded PDPA erasure for this employee — destroys what it can, keeps what statute requires.
detail.directSuperiorSearch: Search by employee ID or name
detail.directSuperiorHint: The reporting and approval hierarchy is derived automatically by following each employee's Direct Superior — no approval levels to configure.
detail.terminateConfirmDescription: This ends {name}'s employment on the chosen date. Assignment history is preserved.
detail.epfElectionHint: Voluntary excess (i-Topup, KWSP Form 17A/18A) sets a rate at or above the statutory 11%/13%; a blank side stays statutory. Rates only — KWSP has no fixed-amount election. Exempt is for legitimately-exempt employees only.
detail.payComponentsHint: Recurring pay items for this employee. Applied to payroll once typed components are enabled.
detail.dateError: Effective end date cannot be before the effective start date.
detail.amountError: Amount must be greater than zero.
detail.currencyUnsupported: Only MYR is supported — payroll is computed in MYR.
detail.epfVoluntaryHint: Enter each side's total rate at or above the statutory floor (employee 11%, employer 12–13%). Leave a side blank to keep it statutory.
detail.epfSemiAutoHint: Enter the employee rate at or above the statutory 11%. The employer side stays automatic (statutory).
detail.gradeMovementOnlyNote: The Grade can’t be changed here. Record it as a movement so it is dated, attributable and shown once on the Employment History:
detail.cp38Hint: CP38 applies by payroll month — periods are month-aligned (a mid-month instruction charges the whole month it starts in) and the amount is deducted in addition to monthly PCB.
detail.cp38ProcessedError: This pay period is already processed — the CP38 record cannot be changed for it.
detail.encashmentUnfreezeConfirmDescription: This re-opens the leave ledger so corrections (e.g. cancelling a booking) can be made. Adjust to re-lock afterwards.
detail.encashmentHint: The effective figure (override, if set, else the auto figure) is what Payroll's leavers panel uses. Adjusting re-locks the balance; a mandatory reason is recorded on both actions.

family.title: Family & Dependents Information
family.note: For benefits and insurance records only. These do not affect payroll or the tax number of children, and are separate from the emergency contact.
family.name: Name
family.hint: HR maintains these records. Employees cannot edit their own family details in this version.
family.childReliefGuidance: LHDN child relief (per child): under 18 — RM2,000; 18+ in full-time pre-university study (e.g. A-Levels, matriculation) — RM2,000; 18+ in diploma/degree study and above — RM8,000; disabled child — RM6,000; disabled child in full-time higher education — RM6,000 plus RM8,000. Claim 100% for one parent, or 50% each when parents share the claim.
family.ageHint: Guidance only: under 18 usually falls under “Child under 18”; 18 and over in full-time study usually falls under a study category. The category is never set automatically — the administrator chooses it.
family.deleteFamilyConfirmBody: This removes the family member from the family register. If child relief is on automatic mode, the employee's child-relief count is refreshed accordingly.

qualification.title: Qualification Information
qualification.deleteConfirmBody: Remove this qualification record? It will no longer appear in this employee's qualification history.
qualification.hint: HR maintains these records. Qualification types are managed under System Settings > System Labels > Profile Options.
qualification.highestHint: Only one record can be the highest qualification. Ticking this moves the marker off the previous record.

clocking.hint: When geofencing is enforced, clock-in/out is blocked unless the employee is within the radius of an assigned site. When off, location is still captured for audit.
clocking.noAssignedSites: No clocking sites are saved for this employee yet. The sites ticked above are proposed from their work location and will be assigned when you press Save. While geofencing is on, their clock-in is refused until at least one is saved.
clocking.noSharedSites: No shared clocking locations exist yet. A group administrator adds them under Attendance › Clocking location.
clocking.linkedPoints: {count, plural, =0 {No clocking point is linked to this employee’s work location yet, so nothing is pre-ticked.} one {# clocking point is linked to this employee’s work location and is pre-ticked.} other {# clocking points are linked to this employee’s work location and are pre-ticked.}} Every shared clocking location is offered in the list above, not only those.

employmentInfo.title: Employment Information
employmentInfo.yearOfServiceTooltip: Group Join Date: {groupJoinDate} · Service as of: {asOf}
employmentInfo.companyChangeableHint: This employee has no transactions yet, so you can still correct their Company here. Choose the correct company, then pick their Department and Save.
employmentInfo.companyPendingBanner: Moving this employee to {company}. Pick their Department and Save to confirm — nothing changes until you Save.
employmentInfo.companyLockedNote: The Company can’t be changed here because this employee already has recorded activity. Use the Movement tab to record a Transfer, which keeps their history intact.
employmentInfo.companyLockedTooltip: Locked — this employee has recorded activity. Use Movement to record a Transfer.
employmentInfo.destinationNotAdministered: You can only move this person to a company you manage. To move them to another company, use the Movement tab to record a Transfer.
employmentInfo.readOnlyNote: Company, Department, Position, Job Grade, Employment Type and Employee Status are shown for reference. Manage them under Movement (transfers) and the Profile tab (grade) to keep their history intact.
employmentInfo.superiorNote: Set the Direct Superior on the card below.
employmentInfo.employeeStatusDerivedNote: Employee Status is worked out automatically from the employment dates and shown as a read-only badge — no manual step.
employmentInfo.blacklistNote: Blacklisting is a deliberate HR action and overrides the automatic Employee Status.
employmentInfo.contractRemarkPlaceholder: e.g. Initial 12-month employment contract. Renewable upon performance review.
employmentInfo.contractNote: Shown for contract employees only. The start date defaults to the Group Join Date until you save one, and the end date is the same date the contract expiry review watches.
employmentInfo.lifecycleDeferredNote: Resignation and last working dates are captured here for records. Wiring them into payroll final pay and attendance cut-off is planned as a follow-up.
employmentInfo.assignmentViewOnlyNote: This information is view-only. Organisation assignment changes are recorded as movement events, so each one keeps its effective date, its reason and its place in the employment history.
employmentInfo.joinDatesViewOnlyNote: Both join dates are view-only. They are set together when the employee is created; afterwards a Join Date Change records a move to another company in the group, and a Group Join Date Correction records an authorised fix to the master service date.
employmentInfo.pendingMovementTitle: Scheduled changes not yet in effect
employmentInfo.pendingMovementNote: The values below are today's. They will not change until each date arrives.

documents.title: Documents
documents.intro: Central repository for this employee's supporting documents. Upload, categorize, view, download, update or remove files. Statutory identifiers are managed on the Bank & Statutory tab.
documents.supportedTypes: Supported: PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, JPG, PNG, TXT (max 10 MB).
documents.confirmDelete: Delete this document? This cannot be undone.
documents.replaceHint: Choose a new file to replace the current attachment

detail.zakatMoved: Zakat has moved to Payroll → Transaction Entry → Zakat.
detail.backupShiftHintFixed: The shift used on any day this employee is not rostered. On a Fixed arrangement that is every working day — roster only the days that differ.
detail.backupShiftHintRoster: The shift used on any day this employee is not rostered. Rostering stays optional: a day with no roster entry falls back to this shift.
detail.shiftTypeHint: Every employee has a backup shift — the shift used on any day they are not rostered. Fixed: they work it every working day, and the roster records only the exceptions. Roster: they are normally scheduled from the Roster screen, and the backup shift covers any day with no roster entry. A dated roster entry always wins; overtime and lateness are measured against whichever shift applies that day. Changing this does not alter attendance already recorded — it changes how days are calculated from now on. The change starts on the effective date you set; days before it keep the shift that was in force then.
detail.shiftEffectiveDateHint: The change starts on the effective date: days before it keep the shift that was in force then.
detail.shiftEffectiveBeforeStart: The effective date cannot be earlier than the employee's start date ({date}).
detail.shiftBackInsertRefused: This employee already has a shift change dated {date}. A change dated before that one cannot be added yet.
detail.shiftHistoryEmpty: No shift change has been recorded for this employee yet.
detail.salaryRevisionConfirmDescription: This adds a new salary record and keeps the full history. It becomes the active salary from the effective date.
detail.salaryAllowanceMovedHint: Allowances are managed in Pay Components under the Payroll module — not on this screen.
detail.salaryInitialEffectiveHint: The first record is effective from the join date.
detail.salaryDeleteConfirmDescription: This removes the record from the salary history and from payroll calculations. Records already used by a closed payroll run cannot be deleted. The removal is kept in the audit trail.
detail.salaryEditConfirmTitle: Save changes to this salary record?
detail.salaryEditConfirmDescription: This edits the latest salary record in place and keeps an audit log of the change.
detail.salaryNoResults: No salary records match your search.
detail.photoHint: PNG or JPG, up to 2 MB.
detail.customHolderHint: Pay this employee's salary into another person's account (for example a spouse or authorised person) when a banking restriction applies. This changes only the payee, never any pay amount.
detail.childReliefAutoSyncNote: Kept in step with the Family records automatically: {count} eligible child(ren). This figure feeds PCB, so it updates on its own whenever a child is added, edited or removed — switch to Manual to set it yourself.
detail.childReliefAutoSynced: Children (PCB Relief) updated automatically to {count} from the Family records.
detail.childReliefAutoSyncedPayrollAlert: Children (PCB Relief) updated automatically to {count} from the Family records — but payroll for {period} is still open. Regenerating that run will now produce a different PCB. Please let the payroll team know.
detail.employerBearsTaxHint: When ticked, the employee's tax (PCB) is still computed and reported in full, but the employer funds it instead of deducting it from net pay. Tax-on-tax gross-up is a follow-up.
detail.icNumberHint: 12-digit MyKad number. Required for Malaysian employees, optional for others. Used to default the SOCSO/EIS and EPF numbers.
detail.icDobInvalidDate: The IC number's first six digits aren't a valid date, so the date of birth wasn't filled in. Enter it manually.
detail.passportHint: Passport number, issue date and expiry date are required for non-Malaysian employees. A Malaysian employee's passport is optional, but the three must be filled together. Issuing country and remark are optional.
detail.recalcHistoryHelp: Automatic adjustments made to this employee’s leave entitlement after a profile change (grade, employment type, hire date or confirmation). “Took effect” is the date the change itself took effect, not the date it was recorded. Where a change took effect in an earlier leave year, the correction applies to the current one and this column shows the date it was posted.
detail.payModeBoundaryError: A pay-mode change must take effect on the first day of a month (the start of a pay period). Salary amount changes may use any date.
detail.payModeBoundaryHint: Pay Mode changes must take effect on the 1st of a month; the daily and hourly modes also need a rate. Basic salary stays the monthly-equivalent wage used for statutory calculations.
detail.paymentMethodBankHint: Bank Transfer requires both a bank name and an account number on the Bank & Statutory tab. Without them the change is rejected, so an unpayable record never reaches the bank file.
detail.payPolicySourceNote: Pay Mode and Payment Term come from the payroll policy <link>{policy}</link> and are shown here for reference. Edit them on the policy so every employee using it stays consistent.

movement.title: Employment History

form.terminateConfirmDescription: This ends the employment on the effective date and closes the current assignment. The action is recorded in the audit trail.
form.comparisonHint: Only the fields you change are recorded. A value left as it is stays untouched and creates no history entry.
form.editHint: Saving a correction rolls this event back and records the corrected version. The original stays in Employment History, marked as corrected — it is never removed.
form.payrollWarning: A processed payroll run already covered this period. Payslips are not reprocessed automatically.
form.joinDateChangeHint: The date you enter becomes the employee’s new Join Date with their current company. Their Group Join Date does not change.
form.groupJoinDateCorrectionHint: The date you enter becomes the employee’s corrected Group Join Date. This is the date years of service is calculated from, so it can change their leave entitlement.
form.confirmationHint: The date you enter is the employee's confirmation date, and any changes on the right take effect from it. Leave the right-hand column untouched to confirm without adjusting salary or anything else.
form.terminationPayrollFlag: Termination saved. A payroll run has already been processed for {periods}, past the termination date — review that run. It was not changed.
form.entityTransferDateHint: This date is when the transfer takes effect, and it also becomes the employee’s Join Date with the company they are moving to. Their Group Join Date does not change, so their service, leave and long-service entitlement carry across.
form.entityTransferHint: Choose the company the employee is moving to. The Business Unit, Department, Position and Work Location lists below now show the destination company’s options — pick a Department there. Their employee ID, Group Join Date and history stay exactly as they are.

movement.rollbackConfirmDescription: The employee's details revert to what they were immediately before this event, and the entry comes off the profile. Nothing is erased — the audit record keeps who did it, when and why, and Show puts the entry back on the list.
movement.rollbackConfirmPayroll: A processed payroll run already covered this period. The rollback will NOT reprocess any payslip — reprocess it separately if that is what you need. The employee's details revert and the entry comes off the profile; nothing is erased, and Show puts it back on the list.
movement.cancelConfirmDescription: This event has not taken effect yet. Cancelling it means it will never apply, none of the employee's details change, and the entry comes off the profile. Nothing is erased — the audit record keeps who did it, when and why, and Show puts the entry back on the list.
movement.payrollLocked: Locked by a closed payroll run
movement.correctedHidden: {count, plural, one {# corrected entry hidden} other {# corrected entries hidden}}

emergency.deleteConfirmBody: Remove this contact? The employee's other emergency contacts are unaffected.
emergency.name: Contact name
emergency.primaryHint: Only one contact can be the primary. Choosing Primary here moves the marker off the previous contact.

detail.disabledIndividualHint: A registered disabled individual is entitled to a further annual tax relief. Setting this to Yes changes the employee's monthly tax: because monthly tax is worked out from the year to date, the month you change it in absorbs the correction for the year so far.
detail.disabledSpouseHint: A registered disabled spouse entitles the employee to a further annual tax relief. This applies only when the tax category is Married & Spouse Not Working — the official rules give it no effect otherwise, so it is recorded and shown but does not change the deduction for any other category. Where it does apply, the month you change it in absorbs the correction for the year so far.
detail.childReliefTableNote: Key the number of children in each official relief category. Use the 100% column when this employee claims the whole relief for that child, and the 50% column when the claim is shared with the other parent — a child in the 50% column is worth exactly half that category’s relief. Whole numbers of zero or more only. The Children (PCB relief) figure above is the total of this table.
detail.locationSuggestionNote: Nothing is saved until you press Confirm. A work location moves payroll and overtime history, so it is never changed for you.
detail.locationBranchUnmapped: {branch} has not been given a work location yet. Map the branch to a location under Attendance › Clocking location and it will be proposed here.
detail.locationNoBranch: No branch is recorded on the Employment tab, so no work location can be proposed from it.
detail.payComponentOverlap: This employee already has a {code} pay component covering {from} to {to}. End that record first, or choose dates that do not overlap it.
detail.payComponentBackwards: This employee already has a {code} pay component starting {from}. A new value must take effect on or after that date.
detail.payComponentMidMonth: A change to the {code} pay component has to take effect on the first of a month. This employee already has a live {code} record covering part of that month, so a change dated part-way through it would pay both records in full. Use {nextFirst}.
detail.payComponentClosedRun: Pay run {period} is closed, so the {code} pay component can no longer be changed for that period.

batch.paymentSummaryTitle: Download a CSV of employee, bank, account and net pay for manual bank upload.

Overtime is keyed as manual ringgit amounts you compute (the system applies no rate) — use the ORP / hourly basis shown for each employee, or Prefill overtime to let the s.60A engine compute it from attendance. Unpaid-leave days are derived automatically from approved unpaid leave.

batch.fieldOtFlatTitle: Flat OT (RM) — any contractual/ex-gratia overtime at the plain hourly rate. Enter the ringgit amount.
batch.fieldOtNormalTitle: Normal working-day OT (RM) — EA s.60A(3): 1.5× the hourly rate for hours beyond normal. Compute and enter the ringgit amount.
batch.fieldOtRestTitle: Rest-day OT (RM) — EA s.60(3): ½-day ORP up to half normal hours, 1 day ORP up to normal hours, then 2× hourly beyond. Compute and enter the ringgit amount.
batch.fieldOtHolidayTitle: Public-holiday OT (RM) — EA s.60D(3): 2 days' ORP at the ordinary rate plus 3× hourly for hours beyond normal. Compute and enter the ringgit amount.
batch.otBasisTitle: EA s.60I(1A) basis for this employee: ORP (ordinary rate of pay) = monthly wages ÷ 26; hourly = ORP ÷ 8. Reference rates: 1.5× normal day, 2× rest day, 3× public holiday. Read-only.

config.title: Statutory Configuration
config.subtitle: The exact Malaysian statutory figures the payroll engine applies — EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB and overtime. Inspect every value with its official source, or publish an effective-dated override.
config.editIntro: Editing legal figures changes FUTURE payroll only — past payslips keep their snapshot. The verified built-in defaults are never lost; they remain the fallback. Bump the version and set an effective date.
config.safetyNote: Wrong values produce wrong, non-compliant payslips. Every figure here is sourced and verified — change it only against an official publication.
config.notesPlaceholder: e.g. EPF employee rate restored to 11% per Budget 2027
config.otMultipliersNote: The 1.5× workday rate and the base-day pay (½/1-day rest-day, 2 days for a public holiday) are fixed by the Employment Act. The rest-day and public-holiday excess-hours rates default to the legal 2× / 3× and can be adjusted here.
config.reliefsPendingSignOffNote: These figures come from a reputable published summary rather than the official document, because the official page is offline. They are the numbers the calculation actually applies. Check each one against the current official publication and confirm it before the first payroll run that relies on it.
config.pcbBands: Tax bands (Table 1: P, M, R, B)
config.bandsReadOnly: Exact agency schedule — {count} bands verified to the RM6,000 ceiling. Maintained as sourced data (a published schedule change is a data update), not hand-edited here.
config.noHistory: No stored overrides. The engine is running on the built-in verified defaults.
config.packsNone: No vendor packs ingested — running on the built-in verified default. Deploy runbook: db:migrate → statutory:sync.
config.staleWarn: A newer statutory pack ({available}) is available but not ingested (latest ingested: {ingested}). Run statutory:sync to apply it.
config.syncFailed: The last sync had {count} failure(s) — check the sync log.
config.perBodySubtitle: Each statutory body resolves its own effective version independently.
config.componentIntro: Publish an effective-dated override for a single body (EPF rates, overtime ceiling, or HRDF rates) without re-issuing the whole ruleset.
config.editSectionIntro: Publish an effective-dated override for this body. The verified defaults stay the fallback; past payslips keep their snapshot.
config.ceilingsNote: Overtime rates are configured under the Attendance module (Shift settings → Overtime rates), not here.
config.bandsEditWarning: Verified PERKESO schedule — edit only for a known statutory change. Wage ranges must ascend without gaps, and amounts are fixed ringgit values, not percentages. A bad edit can be reverted by archiving this version to restore the built-in schedule.
config.socsoCat2: Category 2 — injury only (age 60+ / foreign, employer only)
config.epfPartA: Third Schedule — Part A (citizen / PR, under 60)
config.epfPartE: Third Schedule — Part E (citizen 60 to under 75)
config.epfBandsNote: Amounts are ringgit per wage band, rounded up to the next ringgit. The last row ("and above") is the exact-percentage tail beyond the schedule cap. Leave a row's "Wage to" empty to make it the open-ended top band.
config.epfPartENote: Reduced senior schedule: employee 0%, employer 4%. Applies to Malaysian citizens aged 60 to under 75; no mandatory contribution from age 75.
config.hrdfNote: HRD Corp (PSMB Act 2001) levy rates applied to eligible employers.
config.skbbkDesc: The employee-paid SKBBK (Lindung 24 Jam) contribution schedule — carried on the SOCSO bands and applied by payroll from 1 June 2026.
config.skbbkAbout: SKBBK is an employee-paid leg that rides on the SOCSO contribution bands. It is maintained together with SOCSO — publishing a SOCSO override updates these figures. The employer and SOCSO employee columns are unchanged.
config.skbbkBothCategories: Identical for Category 1 and Category 2 — {count} bands verified to the RM6,000 ceiling. Employees aged 60 and above and foreign workers contribute too.
config.skbbkEditNote: SKBBK amounts are the SKBBK (RM) column of the SOCSO band tables below. Edit them here and publish — the change is saved as a SOCSO statutory version.

fixed.versioningTitle: Changing this item does not overwrite it.
fixed.versioningBody: Saving closes the current value from the effective date you choose and starts a new one, so the history stays intact. Two records for the same pay item can never cover the same day: if your dates run into a record that is already there, the save is refused and the message names it. That means each change adds a line to the list.
fixed.versioningNote: A change adds a line: editing an item closes its current value from the chosen date and starts a new one, so the history stays intact. Two records for the same pay item can never cover the same day.
fixed.deleteHint: Removing an item hides it and excludes it from all future payroll. This stays possible after a pay run has been processed, so a wrong item can be taken out and the run reprocessed. Once a run is closed it can no longer be removed for that period — end it from a date instead, which stops future payments while leaving what was already paid untouched.
fixed.paidOnPayslip: Pay run {period} is closed, so this item can no longer be changed or removed for that period. Reopen the run, or end the item from a date instead — that stops future payments and leaves what was already paid intact.

fixed.backwards: This employee already has a {code} record starting {from}. A new value must take effect on or after that date.
fixed.midMonth: A change to the {code} pay item has to take effect on the first of a month. This employee already has a live {code} record covering part of that month, so a change dated part-way through it would pay both records in full. Use {nextFirst}.

fixed.existingClash: Your dates run into a record above. Saving will be refused — end that record first, or change your dates.

statutoryDetail.basesNotRecordedBody: This payroll run was calculated before the system began saving the wage each statutory body was charged on. The amounts below are exactly what was deducted and paid; the wage behind them cannot be shown, and it is deliberately not guessed from gross pay — an explanation that disagreed with the payslip would be worse than none.
statutoryDetail.basesNotRecordedHeading: The working behind this payslip was not recorded
statutoryDetail.effectiveRateEpfNote: EPF is not a flat percentage of the exact wage. For a monthly wage up to RM20,000 the amount is the figure the KWSP Third Schedule sets for that wage band, rounded up to the next ringgit; only above RM20,000 does the percentage itself apply, and that is rounded up too. A bonus paid in the same month is added to the wage before that band is chosen, so the month is looked up once. The percentage shown here is the effective rate that produced this amount, given for checking only.
statutoryDetail.effectiveRateNote: The percentage is the rate this run actually applied, worked out as the amount divided by the wage recorded above.
statutoryDetail.effectiveRateScheduleNote: The amount comes from the PERKESO contribution schedule for the wage band, not from multiplying by a percentage. The percentage shown is the effective rate that produced it, given for checking only.
statutoryDetail.employerBorneNote: This employer funds part of the employee's statutory share. The Employee column above is the full share as filed with each body; the two lines below show what the company paid and what was really deducted from take-home pay.
statutoryDetail.fieldEmployerBorne: Borne by the employer on the employee's behalf
statutoryDetail.fieldEmployerBorneTotal: Total borne by the employer on the employee's behalf
statutoryDetail.incrementalNote: This is a bonus or off-cycle run, so the amount is only the increase it added on top of what the month had already contributed, while the wage above is the whole month’s. The two do not divide into a rate, so no percentage is shown here.

pcbDetail.additionalMtdMonth: Additional MTD for the whole month
pcbDetail.bracketB: B — tax on M, after rebate
pcbDetail.bracketM: M — first chargeable income of the bracket
pcbDetail.bracketNote: M, R and B are the row of the LHDN tax table that P fell into. A negative B is the RM400 / RM800 rebate.
pcbDetail.bracketTaxOnP: Tax on P for the year
pcbDetail.category3: Category 3 — married and spouse working / divorced / widowed
pcbDetail.compAccNet: Σ(Y − K) — accumulated remuneration after EPF, prior months
pcbDetail.compEpfClaimed: K — EPF already claimed against the annual relief cap
pcbDetail.compK2: K₂ — estimated EPF for each remaining month
pcbDetail.compK2t: K₂ₜ — estimated EPF for each remaining month, re-estimated with the bonus
pcbDetail.compN: n — remaining months after this one
pcbDetail.compY2: Y₂ — estimated remuneration for each remaining month
pcbDetail.currencyNote: Amounts inside the formulas are shown without a currency prefix. They are all in {currency}.
pcbDetail.deltaBanner: This is an off-cycle or bonus run, so the tax deducted on this payslip is the INCREASE in the month's PCB, not the whole month's PCB. The working below is the month's: every figure in it, including the tax bracket and both MTD legs, describes the month with this run's pay included. The increase is shown separately, and it is the amount taken from this payslip.
pcbDetail.deltaEngineRun: Increase the system calculated for this run
pcbDetail.deltaHeading: This run deducted the month's increase
pcbDetail.deltaMonthTotal: PCB for the whole month, as calculated
pcbDetail.deltaNote: The steps above end at the month's PCB, because that is what the recorded working computes. This payslip deducted the difference between the month's PCB and what the month's earlier runs already covered.
pcbDetail.deltaOverrideBanner: This is an off-cycle or bonus run, so the working below describes the whole month rather than this payslip alone, and the tax on this payslip was afterwards entered manually. Three figures are therefore different: the month's calculated PCB, the increase the system worked out for this run, and the amount actually deducted.
pcbDetail.deltaOverrideHeading: This run deducted the month's increase, and it was then set by hand
pcbDetail.deltaOverrideNote: The steps above end at the month's PCB. The increase for this run was worked out from it, and the amount actually deducted was then set by hand — no calculation produced it.
pcbDetail.deltaPrior: PCB the month's earlier runs already covered
pcbDetail.finalPcbDeducted: PCB / MTD actually deducted (set by hand)
pcbDetail.finalPcbMonth: PCB / MTD for the whole month
pcbDetail.finalPcbRun: PCB / MTD deducted on this payslip (the increase)
pcbDetail.flatAdditional: Additional remuneration taxed at the flat rate
pcbDetail.flatNote: A flat rate carries no reliefs, no tax bracket and no accumulators, so there is no relief working to show. That is correct, not a gap.
pcbDetail.flatRemuneration: Remuneration taxed at the flat rate
pcbDetail.flatRoundingNote: The flat-rate amount is truncated to two decimals and then rounded up to the next 5 sen, so the product above lands within 5 sen of the figure beside it rather than exactly on it. Separately, an amount below RM10 is not deducted at all — when that rule bites the figure beside it is nil, however large the product.
pcbDetail.formulaHeading: Monthly tax deduction for the current month
pcbDetail.formulaNet: max( 0, A − Z₁ ) + max( 0, E − max( 0, Z₁ − A ) )
pcbDetail.grossYNote: The accumulator kept for prior months is the remuneration ALREADY net of EPF, Σ(Y − K); the gross Y and its EPF are not stored separately, so they are not shown here rather than being guessed at.
pcbDetail.monthsDivisor: n + 1 — remaining months including this one
pcbDetail.monthsNote: n + 1 is the divisor, so it changes the deduction directly. X includes any amount reported from a previous employer.
pcbDetail.mtdAdditional: Monthly tax deduction on additional remuneration
pcbDetail.mtdNormal: Monthly tax deduction on normal remuneration
pcbDetail.netA: A — normal-remuneration MTD after the RM10 rule
pcbDetail.netE: E — additional-remuneration MTD after the RM10 rule
pcbDetail.netFormulaNote: An MTD below RM10 is not deducted at all, so each leg goes through that rule first — that is what turns the two calculated legs above into A and E. This month's zakat then reduces A, and only what A cannot absorb reaches E. Neither leg can go below zero.
pcbDetail.netLeftover: Zakat left over after the normal leg, applied to the additional leg
pcbDetail.netMtdMonth: Net monthly tax deduction for the whole month
pcbDetail.netMtdNote: The deducted figure is already net of this month's zakat and of the RM10 minimum rule. It is the amount taken from pay and filed with LHDN — nothing on this screen is added to it or taken off it again.
pcbDetail.netMtdRun: PCB deducted on this payslip (the increase)
pcbDetail.netMtdSystem: Net monthly tax deduction the system calculated
pcbDetail.netZ1: Z₁ — zakat paid through salary this month
pcbDetail.noSelection: Open this screen from the PCB / MTD amount on a payslip or on Transaction Detail.
pcbDetail.notFound: That payslip is not available to you, or it no longer exists.
pcbDetail.overrideApplied: PCB deducted after the manual adjustment
pcbDetail.overrideBanner: The tax deduction on this payslip was entered manually, so the working below is not an explanation of it. Everything on this screen describes the figure the system calculated; the amount actually deducted is the adjusted figure.
pcbDetail.overrideHeading: This PCB was set by hand
pcbDetail.overrideNote: The steps above end at the figure the system calculated. The deducted amount was set by hand afterwards, and no calculation produced it.
pcbDetail.p2Formula: P₂ = Σ(Y − K) + (Y₁ − K₁) + (Y₂ − K₂ₜ) × n + (Yₜ − Kₜ) − [ D + S + Du + Su + Q ] − [ ΣLP + LP₁ ]
pcbDetail.p2Note: A month that pays a bonus is calculated twice. P is the year projected on normal remuneration alone; P₂ repeats it with the bonus added and with the projected EPF leg re-estimated as K₂ₜ, because the EPF on the bonus has already used part of the same annual relief cap. The bonus is never added to P itself.
pcbDetail.pFormula: P = Σ(Y − K) + (Y₁ − K₁) + (Y₂ − K₂) × n − [ D + S + Du + Su + Q ] − [ ΣLP + LP₁ ]
pcbDetail.pHeading: P — total chargeable income for the year
pcbDetail.priorPcb: X — accumulated MTD paid, prior months
pcbDetail.reliefFromCurrent: This run predates the recording of the relief legs, so the reliefs shown are the employee's position TODAY, not necessarily the position that was applied. P above is the figure that was actually used.
pcbDetail.reliefFromSnapshot: These reliefs are the ones this payroll run actually applied, recorded when it was calculated.
pcbDetail.roundingNote: The result is truncated to two decimals and then rounded up to the next 5 sen, as the LHDN specification requires. The two zero floors come from the specification too: B carries the RM400 / RM800 rebate as a negative amount, so the tax on P can otherwise fall below zero, and so can this month's share once accumulated zakat and MTD are taken off.
pcbDetail.sourceNote: The statutory table version is the one stamped on this payslip when it ran, not the one in force today.
pcbDetail.step1: Accumulated remuneration after EPF, prior months
pcbDetail.step10: Divide by the remaining months, round up to 5 sen
pcbDetail.step11: MTD on additional remuneration for the month
pcbDetail.step12: Apply the RM10 rule to each leg — below RM10 is not deducted
pcbDetail.step13: Less current month zakat, normal leg first
pcbDetail.step2: EPF already claimed against the annual cap
pcbDetail.step3: Add this month's remuneration, less this month's EPF
pcbDetail.step4: Add the estimated remaining months, less their estimated EPF
pcbDetail.step5: Less individual, spouse, disabled and child relief
pcbDetail.step8: Tax on P for the year
pcbDetail.step9: Less accumulated zakat and accumulated MTD
pcbDetail.subtitle: Every figure the payroll engine used to work out this month's income tax deduction, exactly as it recorded them when the payslip was calculated.
pcbDetail.title: PCB / MTD Calculation Detail
pcbDetail.traceNotRecorded: This payroll run was processed before the full working was recorded, so the steps marked below were never saved for it. They are shown as not recorded rather than as zero, and they are not recalculated — a figure worked out today could differ from the one that was actually deducted.
pcbDetail.unavailable: This payroll run did not record the tax working, so the calculation cannot be shown. Runs calculated from now on record it.
pcbDetail.yearNoAdditional: This month paid no additional remuneration, so the yearly-total step of the calculation did not run.
pcbDetail.yearTotalMtd: Total MTD for the year already accounted for
pcbDetail.yearTotalTax: Total tax for the year on P₂

multiCycleWorksheet.totalsHint: “Paid” is the sum of the figures stored on the payslips. “Each run alone” recomputes every run from the bottom of the bands. “Month as one” treats the month as a single statutory computation. “Movement” is what would change, counted only for the employee-months whose paid figures match “each run alone”.

multiCycleWorksheet.noSkips: Every employee-month with more than one run could be compared.

agents.measuredBody: Every suggestion these agents make is recorded with what happened to it, so their accuracy becomes a measured figure rather than an opinion. Nothing has been recorded yet, because none of them has been switched on — and we would rather show you nothing than a percentage worked out from no evidence.

subStep.yearTypeCompanyDefault: Company default (follow the company leave cycle)
subStep.yearTypeHelp: Types without a choice follow their company's saved leave cycle; picking a value overrides that cycle for this type only.
subStep.earningMappingHelp: Three methods, each doing something different. None hands the entitlement over up front — for Annual Leave a mid-year joiner is still credited only the months remaining in their hire year, and Sick and Hospitalisation leave are credited in full whatever month someone joins. Monthly Accrual earns one twelfth each month, credited on the day you choose. Daily Accrual earns the annual entitlement in daily slices across the leave year, then applies the leave type's rounding rule.
subStep.earningHelp: The earning method is a leave-TYPE setting: one choice here governs every entitlement row under this type, whatever the company or grade. Changing it takes effect on the next grant, accrual run or recalculation.
subStep.roundingHelp: Applied as the final step, AFTER the entitlement calculation — the earning rule itself is unchanged. Choose No Rounding to keep the calculated value exactly, or Custom Rounding and write the table yourself. The rounded figure is the one credited, so it flows through the leave balance, YTD entitled, the entitlement breakdown and the accrual process. Set separately for each leave type.
subStep.carryHelp: Fixed maximum keeps up to the cap; percentage keeps that share of the balance still held at year end. The two are alternatives — with percentage, the percentage alone decides the figure. The expiry fields decide when the carried portion lapses (a date, or X months after year-end).
subStep.carryStepHelp: A front door to the active entitlement policy's carry-forward settings — the per-policy controls under Eligibility remain the underlying truth.
subStep.carryAnnualOnly: Carry-forward applies to Annual Leave — this type's balance does not roll over.
subStep.yearTypeStepHelp: Choose the leave cycle first. The Earning Method and Rounding steps that follow decide how leave is credited within that cycle.
subStep.roundingWorkedExample: With this rule, a calculated {raw} days is credited as {rounded} days.
subStep.roundingCustom: Custom rounding (fill in the table below)
subStep.roundingBandsHelp: Each row covers the decimal part of a calculated entitlement: everything from From up to (but not including) Round To becomes Rounded Result. From is filled in for you — the first row starts at 0.00 and every other row starts where the row above stopped, so the rows always join up. A row of 0.00 / 0.50 / 0.00 turns 10.30 days into 10.00, and a row of 0.50 / 1.00 / 1.00 turns 10.70 into 11.00. Whole figures are never moved, and any decimal your table does not cover keeps its exact value.
subStep.roundingBandRowInvalid: Every row needs a Round To above where the row before it stopped, and both figures must be between 0.00 and 1.00.
subStep.roundingBandOverlap: Two rows cover the same decimals. Ranges must not overlap — the table would have two answers for one figure.
subStep.roundingBandDuplicate: The same range is entered twice. Remove the duplicate row.
subStep.roundingBandGap: Nothing covers {from} to {to}. A calculated value landing in that range keeps its exact decimal.
subStep.earningNotConfiguredNote: This leave type is not configured. It grants nothing and earns nothing — for existing employees, for new joiners, and when anything else triggers a recalculation — until you choose an earning method and save. Saving one then credits everyone on this type the full amount owed, in one upward correction.
subStep.earningLegacyMethodNote: This leave type stores an earning method that is no longer offered. It is shown here read-only and is kept exactly as it is when you save; the calculation still honours it. Choose one of the three current methods to replace it.
subStep.accrualDayHelp: Leave is credited on this day of each month. In a month shorter than the day you pick, it is credited on that month's last day — so 31 credits on 28 February, and on 29 February in a leap year. No month is ever skipped.
subStep.dailyRoundingWarning: Daily Accrual applies your rounding rule to the running total, not to each day's slice, so a rule that rounds a decimal upward will credit a whole day from the employee's very first day. No rounding is the recommended pairing with Daily Accrual.

conditionStep.applicationLimitHelp: Caps the total days an employee may APPLY for of this type in one leave year, whether or not any entitlement balance exists — the rule for types such as Unpaid Leave. It is checked when the application is submitted and again when it is approved. Entitlement, accrual and the balance shown in Leave Summary are untouched. Unlimited is how every leave type behaves today.
conditionStep.maxConsecutiveHelp: Caps how long ONE application of this type may be — a different rule from the yearly maximum above. Calendar Days counts every day the application spans, including weekends and public holidays; Working Days counts only the days actually charged as leave, so a Friday-to-Monday application is 4 calendar days but 2 working days. Checked when the application is submitted and again when it is approved. Where this leave type is also in a Shared Leave Group with its own per-application maximum, the stricter of the two applies and the refusal says which. Unlimited is how every leave type behaves today.
conditionStep.applicationLimitPeriodHelp: A leave year is the same as a calendar year only when your leave year starts in January. Once per employment counts across the whole time someone has worked for you, so a rehire starts fresh.

leave.codeEditableHint: Custom leave codes can be renamed. Use uppercase letters, digits or underscores, starting with a letter (e.g. STUDY_LEAVE). Statutory codes stay locked.
leave.saveConfirmDescription: Save your changes to this leave type?
leave.saveDatabaseError: We could not save this change because of an unexpected system problem. Nothing has been changed. Please try again, and tell your system administrator if it keeps happening.
leave.typesHelp: Statutory minimums come from the country pack (EA 1955; bands are <2 / 2–5 / 5+ years of service) and are not configurable. Grants apply the entitlement you configure — the statutory minimum is shown as guidance and a figure below it is flagged, not overridden. Days are typed in each type's Entitlement step, where each table is effective-dated and an eligibility rule decides who receives it. Annual leave pro-rates in the hire year; sick and hospitalization grant in full.
leave.earnedAccrualHelp: Tops up earned-accrual leave types to today’s accrued balance. Idempotent — safe to run any time.
leave.earnedPreviewEmpty: No earned-accrual entitlement to generate for this scope.
leave.gradesHelp: Seniority bands. Scope a leave policy to a grade to give that grade a different entitlement; ungraded employees use the company default.
leave.gradesToggle: Show or hide the grades list
leave.serviceBandsHelp: Optional — give different entitlements by length of service, above the flat days/year. Bands must cover every service length with no gaps: the first starts at 0, the last is left open-ended. Use "under 2 years", "2 to under 5 years", "5 years and above" phrasing when explaining to staff — e.g. to match a "2–5 years inclusive = 16 days" policy, enter from 2 to 6 (entering to 5 would move an exactly-5-year employee to the next band). The statutory minimum itself steps up after 5 completed years, but it is guidance only — a band below it is flagged, not overridden.
leave.serviceBandsEmpty: No bands — the flat days/year figure above applies to everyone.

leave.carryIncludeEarnedHelp: Include monthly earned balance (saved as configuration)
leave.eligibilityHelp: These rules control both who can see and who can apply for this leave type. Statutory entitlements are never blocked.
leave.eligibilityUndisclosedNote: Employees who haven't disclosed the gated attribute won't see this type — ask them to complete their profile.
leave.eligibilityMultiHint: Select one or more; leave empty to allow everyone.
leave.allowedDurationsHelp: Choose which durations employees may pick for this leave type. Full day is always available.

leave.affectsPayrollDeductionHelp: Set automatically: unpaid leave types reduce pay, paid types do not. This reflects whether the type is paid and cannot be edited here.
leave.payrollImpactHelp: The leave module only flags the impact on approval; the payroll module computes the actual deduction.
leave.backdatingSectionHelp: How many days back from today an employee may apply for this leave type. Leave blank for no limit. HR admins are never blocked by this limit.
leave.perDateApprovalLabel: Allow approving or rejecting individual dates
leave.perDateApprovalHelp: Lets a manager approve some dates and reject others within one multi-day request, instead of an all-or-nothing decision. Only the approved dates are deducted from the balance.
leave.perDateApprovalMultiStepNote: Applies to new requests only, and only when this company uses a single-step approval chain. While a multi-step (manager-then-HR) chain is enabled, such requests fall back to the whole-request flow with no per-date breakdown.
leave.perDateApprovalNoteReplacement: This won't apply to replacement (time-off-in-lieu) leave — those requests always use the whole-request flow.
leave.perDateApprovalNoteCounting: This only takes effect for working-day-counted, full-day leave types. This type is counted differently, so the setting has no effect.

leave.halfDayDeductionHelp: Controls how much leave is deducted when an employee applies leave on a “Half Day” work-schedule day (set on the Shift settings page). Off: deduct 0.5 day. On: deduct 1.0 full day. Full working days are never affected.
leave.halfDayDeductionFrozenNote: Applies to new applications only — leave already submitted or approved keeps the deduction amount shown at the time it was submitted.
leave.encashmentHelp: When an employee's resignation is approved, their unused Annual Leave balance can be frozen and converted into an encashable-days figure for Payroll. This module only calculates and freezes leave days — Payroll handles the ringgit conversion separately.
leave.encashmentRoundingFixed: Rounding: less than 0.5 day rounds down to 0; 0.5 day or more rounds up to the next whole day. The figure never goes below 0.

leave.negativeBalanceNo: No — block applications that exceed the available balance
leave.negativeBalanceHelp: Controls whether an employee can submit or edit a leave application of this type that exceeds their available balance. 'No' blocks over-application at submission and edit (counting leave already pending); 'Yes' allows the balance to go negative.
leave.balanceSourceHelp: Choose which balance an application of this leave type is checked against and deducted from. 'Own Leave Balance' is the default. Pick another leave type and this type keeps no balance of its own: the application is validated against that type's balance and reduces it, while the leave history still shows this leave type. A leave type cannot point at itself, at a type that already deducts from another, or at one that already deducts from this one.

leave.allowUplNo: No — validate the available balance as usual
leave.allowUplHelp: Controls whether an employee may apply for more days than their available balance. 'No' keeps the current behaviour. 'Yes' lets the application through as a single request: the days the balance covers are deducted from this leave type (or from its deduction source), and only the excess is treated as unpaid leave and passed to payroll.

formula.templateHint: Suggested wording, carried over from your first configured leave type. Edit it if this leave type differs — nothing is stored until you press Save.

sharedGroup.title: Shared Leave Groups
sharedGroup.help: A shared leave group lets several leave types draw on one pooled allowance — for example "Special Leave: 10 days a year shared between them, at most 3 days in any one application". A leave type can belong to only one group.
sharedGroup.createHint: Pick at least two leave types — a group needs two to share anything.
sharedGroup.deleteConfirmDescription: The leave types keep their own entitlements; they simply stop sharing one allowance. Leave already taken is not affected.
sharedGroup.errorAlreadyGrouped: {type} already belongs to the shared leave group "{group}". Remove it from that group first.
sharedGroup.errorNameTaken: A shared leave group named "{name}" already exists.
sharedGroup.placementHelp: Choose where this shared group appears on the employee’s Leave tab: as one balance card at the top, lower down with the other leave, or Hidden. This is separate from each leave type’s own placement — hiding a member type never changes the shared balance or what may be applied for. New and existing groups start Hidden.

leave.halfDayDeductionEmptyNote: Selecting no company turns the rule off everywhere: half days deduct 0.5 day again.
leave.maxNegativeBalanceHelp: How far below zero an employee may go. A figure is required when a negative balance is allowed, and it is the floor at BOTH stages: the application is refused if it would pass the limit, and so is the approval. The message says what the limit is and how far past it the request goes.
leave.negativeBalanceNeedsLimitTitle: Leave types allowing a negative balance with no limit set
leave.negativeBalanceNeedsLimitHelp: These leave types are set to allow a negative balance but have no maximum. They behave exactly as they do today — approval still refuses a balance below zero — because the new permission only takes effect once you enter a limit. Work through them: enter a figure where you meant it, or set the switch back to No.
leave.adjustmentsHelp: Add or take away leave days for a group of employees in one action. Choose the leave types, choose who it applies to, then enter the adjustment. Everything you do here is recorded as one action and can be reversed as a unit.
leave.adjustmentsDaysHelp: Half days are allowed, for example 0.5 or 2.5. Whether these days are added or taken away is the adjustment type you chose in step 1.
leave.adjustmentsReasonHelp: This appears on the employee’s leave record, so write what they would need to understand it, for example "CNY 2026 goodwill day".
leave.adjustmentsEmploymentIdsHelp: Paste employee references, separated by spaces, commas or new lines.
leave.adjustmentsEveryoneWarning: No criteria chosen yet. Leaving them all empty means this adjustment applies to EVERY employee. Check the wording on the confirmation before you save.
leave.adjustmentsRecentNone: No adjustments have been made yet.
leave.adjustmentsReverseConfirm: This writes an opposite entry for every record this adjustment created, returning those balances to where they were. Nothing is deleted, and it can only be done once.
leave.overrideSectionHelp: What the system should do when one of the rules above is not met. Choose an action per situation, then switch it on. Nothing changes for this leave type until a rule is switched on. Employees are always told what will happen and must confirm before their application is submitted.

overrideTrigger.advance_notice_not_met: When the minimum advance notice is not met
overrideTrigger.insufficient_balance: When the balance does not cover the application

overrideAction.convert_to_emergency: Offer to submit it as Emergency Leave
overrideAction.split_unpaid: Offer to take the shortfall as unpaid leave

leave.generateHelp: Generate a leave year’s entitlement in five steps: choose the leave types and the year, review how the run behaves, choose who it applies to, read the validation, then process. Nothing is written until you press Generate on the last step.
leave.generateToast: Leave year {year}: {granted} employee(s) granted, {skipped} already granted, {forfeits} forfeit(s) posted.

adjustmentsCriteria.asAtNote: Every criterion here is judged as at the effective date you set in step 3 — not today. Years of service and confirmation status are worked out from the hire and confirmation dates on that date.
adjustmentsCriteria.absentNote: Job Title, Employee Group and Employee Class are not held on the employee record anywhere yet, so they cannot narrow this list. Adding them is its own request.

leave.adjustmentsReviewRecords: {records, plural, one {# record} other {# records}} — {types, plural, one {# leave type} other {# leave types}} × {employees, plural, one {# employee} other {# employees}}
leave.adjustmentsReviewNothing: Nothing to review yet. Go back and choose at least one leave type and at least one employee.
leave.adjustmentsIssuesNone: Nothing to flag — every selected employee can take this adjustment.
leave.adjustmentsIssueNotFound: {count} employee references were not recognised and will be ignored.
leave.adjustmentsIssueInactive: {count} employees were not employed on the effective date. They will still be adjusted.
leave.adjustmentsIssueNotEligible: {count} employees do not qualify for {leaveType} on the effective date.
leave.adjustmentsIssueFrozen: {count} {leaveType} balances are frozen for encashment and will be skipped.
leave.adjustmentsRemarksNote: There is no separate remarks field. The reason above is what the employee sees on their leave record, so write it there.
leave.generateAllTypesNote: Choosing no leave type is a real choice, not an unfinished form: the run then generates every leave type that has entitlement configured, which is what the old Generate button always did.
leave.generateSettingsIntro: These three settings were requested. Here is exactly what this release does about each of them, so nothing on this screen implies a control that is not there yet.
leave.generateSettingProrateNote: Already automatic, and not a decision this run makes. Anyone who joins during the year earns from their join date, on the earning method you configured — whether that was granted at hire or by this run.
leave.generateSettingUntilMonth: Generate leave until a chosen month
leave.generateSettingUntilMonthNote: Not in this release. Capping a year at a month changes how entitlement is calculated, and the joining grant, the monthly accrual and the automatic recalculation all have to learn the same new rule in the same change — otherwise the next profile edit quietly takes the difference back.
leave.generateSettingRecalcNote: Not in this release. It re-does a closed year’s entitlement, its brought-forward balance, its expiry and its forfeits, which moves figures employees have already seen. It arrives with its own preview of exactly what would change and its own separate confirmation.
leave.generateAsAtNote: Every criterion below is judged as at 1 January of the year you chose — not as at today. Someone who has since transferred is selected by where they were then, which is what makes a run reproducible.
leave.generateEveryoneWarning: No criteria chosen yet. Leaving them all empty means this run applies to EVERY employee. Check the matched count below before continuing.
leave.generateMatched: {count, plural, one {# employee selected} other {# employees selected}}
leave.generateValidationHelp: This is a rehearsal of the real run, not a separate checklist: it runs the same calculation and writes nothing. What it says here is what will happen.
leave.generateIssuesNone: Nothing to flag — every selected employee will be granted entitlement.
leave.generateOutcome_unconfigured_method: No earning method chosen for this leave type, so no days can be granted
leave.generateOutcome_already_open: Already granted for this year — it will not be granted twice
leave.generateOutcome_frozen: Balance frozen for encashment, so it will be left alone
leave.generateOutcome_earned_method: Earned monthly, so it accrues through the year instead of being granted now
leave.generateOutcome_no_entitlement: No entitlement configured for this employee and leave type
leave.generateOutcome_pack_blocked: This employee’s company has no active country rules, so nothing can be calculated
leave.generateDecidedByTitle: Which entitlement rule decided each employee
leave.generateDecidedByNote: From the new entitlement rules. These do not decide anybody’s days yet — they are shown so you can check them before they take over.
leave.generateDecidedBySoleLine: {template} — the only entitlement table for this leave type, so no rule was needed
leave.generateReviewTypeCount: {count, plural, one {# leave type} other {# leave types}}
leave.generateProcessNote: Pressing Generate writes the entitlement. Running it again later is safe — anyone already granted for this year is skipped rather than granted twice.
leave.generateNothingToProcess: Nothing to process yet. Go back and choose a year and at least one employee.
leave.generateRunsNone: No entitlement has been generated yet.
leave.generateRunsLine: {selected} selected · {passed} passed · {failed} failed · {granted} records granted · {forfeits} forfeit(s)

holidays.pageDescription: Holidays used by leave and attendance working-day counting
holidays.addHint: Holidays are matched by country and date. A day marked here is excluded from working-day leave counts and classifies attendance as a public holiday.
holidays.deleteGroupInUse: This holiday group is still assigned to employees. Reassign them before deleting it.
holidays.groupEmpty: No holiday groups yet. Create one to assign a multi-state calendar to staff.
holidays.groupsHint: A group is a named bundle of states. Assign it to a staff member on their profile so the correct state holidays apply. Hold Ctrl (or Cmd) to select multiple states.
holidays.archetypeHint: Standard = official gazetted holidays only (national + the group’s states). Extended = official holidays plus company-defined extra days. Custom = only the holidays you hand-pick into this group; every other date, including national holidays, is a normal working day. Assign a group to staff on their profile (or map it to a location) and they follow exactly these rules.
holidays.parentGroupHint: A group with a parent automatically inherits the parent’s whole calendar — its gazette states, kind and extra days — and stays in sync when the parent changes. Add days that apply only to this group by adding a holiday with the “Holiday group” scope. One level of inheritance only: a parent cannot itself inherit from another group.
holidays.calendarEmpty: No holidays in this calendar yet.
holidays.calendarHint: Inherited days are read-only here — edit them at their source (the parent group, the public holiday list or the owning company). Days added to this group apply only to staff on this calendar.
holidays.editHint: Change any detail here and Save. Country stays as recorded. Leave and attendance follow the saved holiday automatically.
holidays.nationalStateHint: National applies to everyone. Choose a state to apply this holiday only to staff working in that state.
holidays.scopeFixedHint: This holiday belongs to a business group or holiday group. Its National / State cannot be changed here.

users.title: Users & roles
users.provisioningNote: New logins are created by invitation only — there is no open sign-up. An admin invites an existing employee by email, then WorkOS sends the one-time link and the invitee sets their own password. Only group admins can invite, archive or restore a login. Archiving blocks access without deleting anything, and a login is blocked automatically once every employment of that person has ended. Company scope applies to HR Admin grants — that company and its sub-companies; other roles are group-wide.
users.inviteHint: New accounts are created by invitation only — there is no open sign-up. The person receives a one-time email link to set their password.
users.functionAccessCaption: Which role can reach each screen. This mirrors the access the system enforces; it is a reference view, not an editor — changing enforcement lives in the role guards and database policies.

scope.people: Everyone can open this; the list is limited to the people you are allowed to see.
scope.leave: Everyone can open this; you see your own leave, managers and admins see their reports.
scope.leaveTracker: Everyone can open this; you see your own leave, managers see their reports, and administrators get the employee lookups instead of the calendar.
scope.attendance: Everyone can open this; you see your own attendance, managers and admins see their reports.
scope.approvals: Managers and above; what appears follows your actual reporting lines.
scope.roster: Managers and above; what appears follows your actual reporting lines.
scope.performance: Managers and above; what appears follows your actual reporting lines.
scope.leaveApproval: Managers and admins; what appears follows your actual reporting lines.
scope.payrollConfig: Everyone can open this; only admins for the company can change it.
scope.delegations: HR and admins see every delegation; you see only ones you delegated or cover.
