onboarding.welcomeBody: A quick 30-second tour of where everything lives. You can replay it any time from the help button in the top bar.
onboarding.navBody: Every module lives in this sidebar. What you see here depends on your role — employees, managers and HR admins each get their own tools.
onboarding.workspaceBody: Your personal hub: profile, payslips, leave balance and attendance — everything about you, in one place.
onboarding.kbBody: Step-by-step guides for every module, plus your company’s policies and documents. Start here whenever you’re unsure how something works.
onboarding.approvalsBody: As a manager, requests from your team — leave, attendance and profile changes — wait for your decision here.
onboarding.adminBody: Set up your company, departments and people, configure leave and payroll, manage roles, and review the audit trail. New here? Open the “Getting Started” guide in the Knowledge Base.
onboarding.languageBody: Use the app in English, 简体中文, Bahasa Melayu, தமிழ், ไทย or Tiếng Việt — your choice is remembered.
onboarding.themeBody: Toggle between light and dark themes to suit your eyes and your room.
onboarding.finishBody: That’s the tour. Whenever you need a hand, open the Knowledge Base or replay this tour from the help button.

intro.title: Your self-service home
intro.body: This is your personal hub. We'll walk through your profile, bank and statutory details, payslips, and your leave and attendance summary.

contact.title: Your contact details
contact.body: Update your phone, address, date of birth, and emergency contact here. These changes save **immediately**, no approval needed.

bank.title: Bank and statutory
bank.body: Your bank account and PCB tax category live here. Open **Request a change** to submit edits, which go to your admin for approval.

payslips.title: Your payslips
payslips.body: Every pay period lands here. Click a period to open the full payslip and download it.

attendance.title: Attendance summary
attendance.body: Check in and out for today from here. For your full attendance history, open the Attendance page. You can also request a fix for a missed punch.

leave.title: Leave balances and requests
leave.body: See what's accrued, used, and available across leave types. Use **Request leave** to file a new application.

intro.title: Leave walkthrough
intro.body: Welcome to Leave. We'll show you your leave balances, how to request time off, and where requests are tracked.

balance.title: Check your balance
balance.body: This table shows how much leave you have left, broken down by type. Available days appear over your total entitlement.

request.title: Request leave
request.body: Open this panel to fill in the dates, leave type, and reason, then submit your request for approval.

config.title: Configure leave types
config.body: Admins set up leave types, entitlements, and the leave year here. This is where policies and holidays are managed.

intro.title: Tour the attendance page
intro.body: This quick walkthrough covers checking in and out, reading daily status, your record, and submitting a correction request.

day.title: Your daily record
day.body: This card lists everyone for the selected day, with check-in, check-out, hours, and overtime. Use the date nav up top to move between days.

action.title: Check in and out
action.body: Each row's action enters a time and **checks you in**, then later **checks you out**. Once both are set, the day is marked done.

status.title: Present, late, half day
status.body: The status pill shows present, late, half day, or absent for the day. On leave, holidays, and rest days appear here too.

correction.title: Request a correction
correction.body: Wrong time logged? Submit a correction request with the proposed times and a reason, then a manager approves or rejects it.

summary.title: Your monthly summary
summary.body: Scroll down for the month roll-up: present, late, half day, leave, absent days, plus hours and overtime flags. That wraps up the tour.

intro.title: Run a payroll cycle
intro.body: This walkthrough covers running payroll: creating a payroll process, reviewing payroll processes, and finding statutory reports like EA and CP39.

batches.title: Your payroll processes
batches.body: Every pay run lives here. Click a period to open a payroll process and review payslips, net pay, and statutory totals.

create.title: Create Payroll Run Cycle
create.body: Click **Create Payroll Run Cycle** to open the guided wizard: pick the period and cycle, choose employees, then review and process.

reports.title: Statutory reports
reports.body: This is where EA, Form E, CP39, and monthly EPF/SOCSO/EIS statutory reports are generated.

worklist.title: Compliance worklist
worklist.body: Track CP22 and CP22A obligations here so new hires and leavers are notified to LHDN on time.

generate.title: Generate a report
generate.body: Choose a company, report, and period, then click **Preview** to review figures before exporting or recording.

intro.title: People and org tour
intro.body: This quick walkthrough shows you how to find people, hire, and manage your organization's master data. Let's start on the People page.

search.title: Search for people
search.body: Type a name or email here and hit **Search** to filter the directory. Use **Clear** to reset back to everyone.

table.title: Browse the directory
table.body: Every employee shows here with their department, company, and status. Click a name to open their full profile.

hire.title: Create new employee
hire.body: Click **+ Create new employee** at the top right. It opens a step-by-step screen — you can save a draft at any point and finish it later. For bulk onboarding, use **Import employees** with the Excel template.

orgTree.title: Your group structure
orgTree.body: Admins manage org master data here. This tree shows how your companies nest into a group.

orgCompanies.title: Companies and master data
orgCompanies.body: Open any company to manage its details, statutory identity, and bank profiles. Use **Add company** below to register a new one. The shared lists — departments, positions, cost centers — now live under System Labels.

intro.title: System Labels
intro.body: This is where you set up the shared lists everyone else picks from — departments, positions, cost centers and business units for each company, plus your organisation-wide grades.

companies.title: Per-company catalogs
companies.body: Open a company to add, edit, archive or delete its departments, positions, cost centers and business units. Each can carry an optional description. Grades are organisation-wide and are maintained from the same screen.

intro.title: Performance reviews tour
intro.body: This quick walkthrough shows how to run performance review cycles, handle reviews awaiting you, and open or create a cycle.

pending.title: Reviews awaiting you
pending.body: When team reviews need your input they appear here. Click **Review** on any row to complete it.

cycles.title: Review cycles
cycles.body: Every cycle is listed here with its period, status, and progress. Click a cycle name to open it and manage its reviews.

newCycle.title: Create a new cycle
newCycle.body: Expand this panel to set the name, scope, period, and merit pool, then click **Create cycle** to launch it.

intro.title: Your approvals inbox
intro.body: This is the one place where everything awaiting your decision lands — leave, attendance corrections and profile changes. Let's walk through how to clear it.

header.title: Pending at a glance
header.body: The header shows how many requests are still pending across all queues. When it hits zero, your inbox is clear.

leave.title: Leave requests
leave.body: Each pending leave request shows the employee, type, dates and days. Review the details before you decide.

decide.title: Approve or reject
decide.body: Use the buttons in this column to **approve** or **reject** a request. You can't approve your own — those rows show *Your request* instead.

corrections.title: Attendance corrections
corrections.body: Punch-time fixes appear here. RLS already trims every queue to what you're allowed to see, so you only decide within your scope.

intro.title: Tour the org chart
intro.body: This quick walkthrough shows how to **search**, **collapse and zoom**, and read the reporting lines that connect your team.

header.title: Your org at a glance
header.body: The header names this view and shows how many people are mapped. Everyone reports up from here.

search.title: Find anyone fast
search.body: Type a name, role, or department in the **search** box at the top right. Matches light up and scroll into view, even inside collapsed branches.

controls.title: Collapse and zoom
controls.body: Click the **+/− toggle** under any manager to collapse or expand their reports. Use the **zoom buttons** to fit large teams on screen.

lines.title: Read the reporting lines
lines.body: Each connector style means a different relationship. Check this **legend** to tell direct, functional, project, and dotted-line reporting apart.

intro.title: Admin walkthrough
intro.body: This tour covers managing user roles, assigning and revoking access, scoped company admins, and the audit trail. Let's start with users.

users.title: Your users
users.body: Every person in the system is listed here with their current roles. Each tag shows a role and, when scoped, the company it applies to.

assign.title: Assign a role
assign.body: Pick a role, optionally scope it to a company, then click **Add role**. Use the **×** beside a tag to revoke access.

provisioning.title: Scoped admins
provisioning.body: Company-scoped **hr_admin** roles let delegated admins manage only their own subtree. This note explains how provisioning and scope work.

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.body: Now jump to the audit log. Filter by record type, search events, or narrow a date range to find exactly what changed.

auditTable.title: Every change, logged
auditTable.body: Each row is one event from the immutable log — who did what, when. That's the admin tour; you're all set.

claims.title: Claims
claims.subtitle: Submit an expense or benefit claim and track its status.
claims.noTypes: No claim types are configured yet. Ask your HR admin to add them.
claims.cancelConfirmDescription: This withdraws the claim. You can submit a new one.
claims.noEmployment: No active employment is linked to your account, so you cannot submit claims.
claims.draftHint: A draft holds none of your claim limit until you submit it.
claims.draftsHint: Saved but not yet submitted. Tick the ones you want to file and submit them together.
claims.submitSelectedHint: All selected drafts are submitted together, or none are.
claims.deleteDraftConfirmDescription: The draft and any receipt attached to it are removed. This cannot be undone.
claims.mileagePricedOnSubmit: The amount is worked out from the mileage rate table when you submit.

analytics.title: HR analytics
analytics.description: Headcount, hiring, attrition and master-data exports for the selected period.
analytics.turnoverFormula: Turnover rate = leavers ÷ average headcount × 100. Average headcount = (start + end) / 2.
analytics.masterDataDesc: Download the active employee roster. Compensation columns are admin-only.
analytics.pdfNonLatinNote: PDF is a human-readable summary; non-Latin names (e.g. CJK, Tamil) appear as “?”. Use Excel or CSV for the lossless export.
analytics.sickNotConfigured: No sick-leave type is configured for this tenant.
analytics.nationalityFootnote: Nationality uses EPF citizenship as a proxy; it defaults to Citizen when unset.
analytics.carryForwardDesc: Annual-leave amounts brought forward into each leave year, their expiry date, and what was forfeited — at year/cycle open (exceeded the carry-forward limit) and at expiry (unused brought-forward days lapsed).

payComponents.title: Pay Items
payComponents.description: Define configurable pay items and their statutory treatment (EPF / SOCSO / PCB / HRDF).
payComponents.previewNotice: Preview. The catalog is ready to use; payroll switches to typed components only when enabled (TYPED_PAY_COMPONENTS_ENABLED). Until then payroll runs on basic + allowance + overtime + bonus as today.
payComponents.archiveDescription: Deactivate {code}? It will no longer be available to add — you can reactivate it later.
payComponents.empty: No pay items found — adjust the search/filter, or seed the Malaysia defaults to start.
payComponents.flagsHint: Flags decide which statutory base the component feeds. Non-Payable items and PCB-only earnings are not computed in this version.
payComponents.epfConfigTip: Controls how this pay code feeds the EPF (KWSP) contribution. EPF Bonus 2012 marks it as a bonus payment under the EPF bonus contribution rules.
payComponents.epfBonus2012Tip: Treat this pay code as a bonus payment for EPF: the amount is added to the month's wage and the EPF statutory table is read once for the total, so the employer rate follows the whole month (EPF Bonus 2012 rules). Requires EPF to be ticked.
payComponents.pcbConfigTip: Classifies this pay code for Monthly Tax Deduction per the LHDN Spesifikasi Pengiraan PCB 2026 Menggunakan Pengiraan Berkomputer.
payComponents.remunerationTypeTip: How the pay code enters the PCB calculation (LHDN PCB 2026 specification): Normal remuneration, Additional remuneration, or an Optional Deduction that reduces the monthly tax.
payComponents.exemptionTypeTip: The LHDN exemption or optional-deduction code with its yearly limit (RM). The list follows the selected Remuneration Type: PCB codes for Normal/Additional, LP codes for Optional Deduction.
payComponents.errorStatutory_pcbRemunerationTypeRequir: Remuneration Type is required when PCB is ticked.
payComponents.errorStatutory_pcbExemptionTypeRequired: Exemption Type is required when PCB is ticked.
payComponents.errorStatutory_pcbExemptionTypeInvalid: The selected Exemption Type does not belong to the chosen Remuneration Type.
payComponents.errorStatutory_epfBonusRequiresEpf: EPF Bonus 2012 requires the pay code to be subject to EPF.
payComponents.errorUnsupportedTaxable: Pay code "{code}" is marked Non-payable and subject to PCB but has no Remuneration Type. Payroll cannot calculate the tax on it, so this combination cannot be saved. Untick PCB, or choose a Remuneration Type.
payComponents.recordOnlyNote: Record only — does not affect take-home pay.
payComponents.sectionEaFormHint: Where this pay item's money is reported on the C.P.8A (EA). It changes no calculation and no statutory flag. The EA form itself says which years a mapping is not yet in effect for.
payComponents.deleteDescription: Permanently delete {code}. Blocked if any employee or payroll run uses it — deactivate instead.
payComponents.searchPlaceholder: Search pay code, label or description…
payComponents.errorInUse: This pay item is used by {refs} record(s) — deactivate it instead of deleting.
payComponents.errorCodeDuplicate: Pay code {code} already exists — pay codes must be unique.
payComponents.errorCodeDuplicateArchived: Pay code {code} exists but is deactivated — reactivate it instead.
payComponents.inputTypeLinkTitle: Open {code} to change its Input Type
payComponents.sectionPaySettingsHint: How the amount is worked out — rounding, Input Type and the Formula builder.
payComponents.displayCategoryHint: Decides which box this item appears in on payslips, payroll results, transaction view and payroll reports. It changes nothing else — no statutory calculation, and no EA, CP39, KWSP or PERKESO figure. Leave it on “Work it out automatically” to keep the box worked out for you, as before.
payComponents.sectionOrpHint: Choose whether this pay item is included when the ordinary rate of pay is worked out. The two boxes are independent — tick either, both or neither. The ORP formula itself is unchanged; these boxes only decide which pay items feed it.
payComponents.orpUnpaidLeaveLabel: Add to Unpaid Leave ORP Calculation
payComponents.orpUnpaidLeaveHint: Today the unpaid-leave and absence daily rate is worked out from basic salary alone. Tick this to add this pay item to that base. It also lowers the EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB and HRDF bases, because the unpaid-leave deduction is taken before those are worked out.
payComponents.orpOvertimeHint: Counts this pay item towards the "All fixed allowances" total your overtime formula reads. Until now that was decided by the item’s Category instead; every item was ticked on release day so nobody’s overtime changed.
payComponents.orpDeductionWarning: This pay item is a Deduction. Malaysian employment law works overtime out from the ordinary rate of pay derived from wages, so a deduction is not taken off that base. Your choice is saved, but it does not lower anyone’s overtime or unpaid-leave rate. Tell us if you need this to change.
payComponents.orpStatutoryNote: Statutory overtime worked out from attendance is not affected by these boxes. It is based on the Basic Salary and Monthly Allowance on the employee’s Personnel record.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.ariaBell: Notifications, {total} waiting: {unread} unread and {tasks} open tasks

approvalHistory.title: Approval History
approvalHistory.description: Recent decisions on your team's requests — including those made by a stand-in on your behalf.

payrollConfig.title: Payroll configuration
payrollConfig.description: Per-company payroll schedule and statutory employer identity.
payrollConfig.emptyScope: No companies in the current scope. Use the company switcher above.
payrollConfig.dayHint: Day of month (1–31). Leave blank for month-end. Scheduling reference only — it does not change how the pay period is calculated.
payrollConfig.hrdfHint: Registration numbers appear on statutory files and payslips.
payrollConfig.cutOffsHint: Day of month (1–31). Blank = month-end. The salary/inputs cut-off is set above as Cut-off day. These are the COMPANY DEFAULT cut-off windows: payroll pulls each transaction type (overtime, claims, unpaid leave, attendance) from its configured window when an employee's payroll policy doesn't set its own. Statutory contributions still aggregate per calendar month.
payrollConfig.defaultPolicyHint: Applied to every employee who has no payroll policy assigned individually.
payrollConfig.releaseHint: Controls when employees can see their payslip in self-service. Fixed day = a day of the month after the pay period; relative = days before(-)/after(+) pay day. Never before payroll closes.
payrollConfig.statutoryReadOnlyHint: Shown for reference only. These employer registration details are one record with one owner — Organization → Statutory. They used to be editable here as well, so whichever screen saved last silently won.
payrollConfig.movedSettingsHint: Probation length, review reminders and the default salary currency are not payroll settings and have moved:
payrollConfig.listDescription: Choose a company to view or change its payroll timing.

errors.invalidDefaultPolicy: The chosen default payroll policy must be an active policy in this company.

employeeIdConfig.title: Employee ID Auto Running Number Setup
employeeIdConfig.description: Define how new Employee IDs are generated — prefix, starting number, digits and scope.
employeeIdConfig.gapNotice: Employee IDs are guaranteed unique but not strictly gap-free: deleted employees, manually keyed IDs, or replacing a setup can leave gaps in the sequence.
employeeIdConfig.empty: No Employee ID setups yet. Create one to auto-generate Employee IDs at hire.
employeeIdConfig.deleteDescription: The "{prefix}" numbering setup will be removed. Existing employees keep their IDs.
employeeIdConfig.fieldScopeHint: Global shares one sequence across all companies; company-specific keeps a separate sequence per company.
employeeIdConfig.fieldPrefixHint: Letters, numbers and dashes. Prefix + digits + suffix together must be at most 30 characters.
employeeIdConfig.fieldCurrentHint: The last number issued. The next hire receives the following number.

errors.duplicateActive: An active Employee ID setup already exists for this scope
errors.prefixCollision: Another active setup already uses this prefix
errors.tooLong: Prefix, number length and suffix together must be at most 30 characters

employeeIdConfig.fieldTemplateNameHint: Optional label so several numbering formats can run side by side.
employeeIdConfig.fieldSuffixHint: Optional text after the number, e.g. MY → EMP0001MY. Letters, numbers and dashes.
employeeIdConfig.fieldLengthHint: Leading zeroes: the number is padded to this many digits.
employeeIdConfig.fieldAllowManualOverrideHint: When on, HR may hand-key an Employee ID (checked for uniqueness) instead of auto-generating it.
employeeIdConfig.cp39LengthNote: Note: Employee IDs longer than 10 characters do not fit the LHDN CP39 submission file — CP39 generation will list the affected employees instead of truncating. Longer IDs remain fully usable everywhere else.

payrollPolicy.title: Payroll policies
payrollPolicy.description: Named, reusable rules for how each employee's payroll is processed. Assign a policy to an employee and payroll applies it automatically.
payrollPolicy.previewNotice: General Settings below (proration, negative net pay, overtime caps, leave divisors, rounding) are live and applied during payroll calculation. Statutory minimums (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB, and the EA 1955 overtime floor) always stay locked and cannot be set below the law. Custom-period cut-off windows are recorded but not yet applied to calculation.
payrollPolicy.typeDefaultHint: The policy type and payment frequency here are template defaults for new assignments. An existing employee's Pay Mode and Payment Term are set on their Basic Salary record (Personnel → Payroll tab).
payrollPolicy.emptyScope: No companies in the current scope. Use the company switcher above.
payrollPolicy.deleteDescription: Delete the policy "{name}"? This cannot be undone.
payrollPolicy.typeHint: Monthly and Daily are applied to payroll. A Daily policy pays its per-day rate for the eligible days worked in the period — monthly proration does not apply. Hourly is configurable now (rate plus shift-schedule setting) but its live payslip generation is a signed-off follow-up. Custom-period is configurable now (a cut-off window with an anchor day); applying that window to overtime, attendance and leave is a signed-off follow-up.
payrollPolicy.assignHint: Payroll uses the assigned policy automatically on the next run. Leave on the default for standard monthly processing.
payrollPolicy.assignInactiveNote: The assigned policy is inactive, so payroll falls back to the monthly default.

errors.duplicateName: A payroll policy with this name already exists for this company.
errors.inUse: This policy is assigned to employees and cannot be deleted. Unassign it first.
errors.companyMismatch: A payroll policy can only be assigned to employees in its own company.
errors.defaultInUse: This payroll policy is set as a company default and cannot be deleted.

payrollPolicy.dailyHint: Daily policies pay a per-day rate for the days worked in the period; monthly proration does not apply. The per-day rate is required for a Daily policy.
payrollPolicy.fieldOnlyWithinShift: Only pull hours within shift schedule
payrollPolicy.onlyWithinShiftHint: When on, only hours worked within the employee's assigned rostered shift are payable. Hours clocked outside the shift, overtime beyond the shift, and any day with no rostered shift are excluded. When off, all worked hours count.
payrollPolicy.hourlyHint: Hourly policies pay a per-hour rate for the hours worked in the period. The per-hour rate is required for an Hourly policy. Live end-to-end hourly payslip generation is a signed-off follow-up; today an Hourly policy stores its rate and shift-schedule setting and can be assigned, but is not yet applied to a payroll run.
payrollPolicy.customPeriodHint: Custom-period policies record a cut-off window — an anchor day for a non-calendar pay period. Choose "Custom period" and set the anchor day to store the window. The window is saved and validated now, but is not yet applied to a payroll run (applying it to overtime, attendance and leave is a signed-off follow-up). Statutory months (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB) always stay on the calendar month by law and are never moved by the window.

cutOff.title: Cut-off window
cutOff.anchorDayHint: Used only for the "Custom period" mode. The anchor day (1–28) is the day of the month the window opens — for example, anchor 25 means the window runs from the 25th of the previous month to the 24th of the period month. Applies only to Custom-period policies; statutory months stay on the calendar month.
cutOff.frequencyHint: How often payroll runs. Weekly and bi-weekly are operational cadences — statutory contributions (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB) are still aggregated and reported per calendar month, as required by law.
cutOff.perTypeHint: Each transaction type can close on its own anchor day (1–28). Leave blank to inherit the salary anchor day above. Only used when the period mode is "Custom period".
cutOff.previewHint: The dates each transaction type will be picked up for the current month, derived from the saved cut-off configuration. Consecutive periods are contiguous and never overlap.
cutOff.perFrequencyHint: When the payroll frequency is Weekly or Bi-Weekly, that frequency can use its own anchor day and per-type cut-off days. Leave blank to inherit the Monthly (base) cut-off above. Only used when the period mode is "Custom period".
cutOff.scheduleHint: The cut-off cycles this payroll frequency generates for the month. Weekly and bi-weekly split the month into contiguous cycles; statutory contributions are still aggregated per calendar month by law.

config.salaryIncrementProration: Split a mid-month salary increment across the two rates
config.prorationHint: Used when a joiner/leaver works part of the month. Default (calendar days) reproduces today's figures.
config.salaryConfigHint: Configure the basic-salary formula for each employee event independently. Leaving an event at "default" inherits the basis above.
config.incrementHint: When on, a mid-month pay raise is split day-by-day across the old and new rate.
config.negativeCarryForward: Carry the balance forward to the next cycle
config.negativeNetHint: "Carry forward" holds this cycle's net at zero and recovers the shortfall from the next cycle's net pay.
config.otExceedConvert: Convert the excess to a pay item
config.otHint: The multiplier is floored at the statutory 1.5×. Convert redirects any overtime above the cap onto the chosen pay item so it is still paid.
config.deductAbsentDaysHint: A scheduled working day with no attendance record, or one marked Absent, is deducted at the same daily rate as unpaid leave, before EPF, SOCSO, EIS and PCB. Approved leave, public holidays and rest days are never counted, and the roster wins over the company calendar. Off by default; it applies only to payroll runs made after it is turned on.
config.leaveHint: Divisors decide how one unpaid day / encashed day is valued. Default (calendar month) reproduces today's figures.
config.roundingHint: Statutory contribution rounding always follows its own legislated rules and is unaffected.

wizard.requiredHint: Complete the required fields on this step to continue.
wizard.reviewHint: Review the configuration below, then Save. Use Previous to return to any step and amend.
wizard.reviewDraftNote: Saved as a draft, this policy is not applied to payroll. Activate it from the policy list when ready.

validation.name: Policy name is required.
validation.dailyRate: Enter a per-day rate greater than zero.
validation.hourlyRate: Enter a per-hour rate greater than zero.

leaveApproval.description: Choose who signs off on leave, and in what order, for each company.
leaveApproval.empty: No steps yet — add at least one.
leaveApproval.archiveConfirm: Delete this rule? Requests already in progress keep their current approval chain.
leaveApproval.noRules: No scoped rules yet. All requests use the default chain above.
leaveApproval.templatesHint: Reusable approval chains you build once and assign to many leave types and companies.
leaveApproval.deleteTemplateConfirm: Delete this template? It must not be assigned anywhere first.
leaveApproval.tenantDefaultHint: Applies automatically to every company and leave type with no specific rule.
leaveApproval.assignmentsHint: Map a template to many leave types and companies in one step.
leaveApproval.noTemplates: No templates yet — add one to reuse it across leave types.
leaveApproval.unassignConfirm: Remove this assignment? The leave type falls back to the default chain.
leaveApproval.rolesGatedNote: Steps route as follows: Department Head / Business Unit Head go to the head set for that unit under Settings → System Labels (a head step is skipped when no head is set); HR and HR Manager go to HR admins; Payroll goes to payroll partners; Custom Role goes to an HR admin. An HR admin can also clear any step, so a chain always completes.
leaveApproval.workflowsHint: Every configured approval workflow. Open one to see or change its steps and conditions.
leaveApproval.noWorkflows: No workflows configured yet. Requests use the company default chain.
leaveApproval.workflowTypeAutoHint: Approvers follow the employee's reporting line automatically — no level-by-level setup needed.
leaveApproval.advancedOverrideHint: Use a template or build a custom approval chain that diverges from the reporting line.
leaveApproval.workflowTypeDefaultHint: Use a ready-made template. No level-by-level setup needed.
leaveApproval.noActiveTemplates: No active templates yet — create one above first.
leaveApproval.saveConfirmBody: Are you sure you want to save this approval workflow configuration?
leaveApproval.escalationHint: Chase a leave request that has sat with an approver for too long.
leaveApproval.escalationNotifyNote: Escalation alerts are delivered to the notification bell.
leaveApproval.templateCreationHint: Build a reusable approval flow and its steps here.
leaveApproval.multiStepNote: A template with two or more steps is a multi-step approval; a one-step template is a single approver. The template you assign decides — there is no separate company switch.
leaveApproval.assignmentTemplateHint: Decide which companies, leave types and employees each approval flow applies to.
leaveApproval.noEligibilityRules: No eligibility rules for the chosen companies.
leaveApproval.ruleNotAssignable: This rule narrows by something an approval flow cannot scope on. Use a rule based on company, employment type and grade group.
leaveApproval.legacyGradeScope: Assigned by grade — re-assign by eligibility rule
leaveApproval.escalationSectionHint: Chase an approval that has stalled. Set per company — open the one you need.

taxRelief.title: Personal Tax Relief (TP1)
taxRelief.intro: Declare your total optional personal tax reliefs (LHDN form TP1) for an assessment year. The latest submitted amount reduces your monthly tax deduction (PCB/MTD).
taxRelief.amountHelp: Enter the total optional reliefs you intend to claim for the year — for example life insurance, medical, lifestyle, and education fees. This is a single annual amount.
taxRelief.submittedNotice: This year has been submitted. The latest submitted amount feeds your payroll. To change it, submit a correction.
taxRelief.historicalDraft: Saved as a draft for this assessment year.
taxRelief.historicalNone: No declaration was made for this assessment year.
taxRelief.historyNote: Previous submissions are kept and visible in your record history. Past assessment years are shown read-only.
taxRelief.totalNote: Your annual total is calculated automatically from the categories above when you save or submit.
taxRelief.remarksPlaceholder: Any notes or declaration for HR (optional).

individual.label: Individual and dependent relatives (RM)
individual.help: Standard individual relief and dependent relatives. Statutory cap RM 9,000.

spouse.label: Spouse / alimony (RM)
spouse.help: Relief for a non-working spouse or alimony payments. Statutory cap RM 4,000.

children.label: Children (RM)
children.help: Total qualifying-child relief for the year.

parent.label: Parents (RM)
parent.help: Medical, care or examination expenses for your parents.

medicalInsurance.label: Medical / insurance (RM)
medicalInsurance.help: Life and medical insurance, EPF, and approved medical expenses.

lifestyle.label: Lifestyle (RM)
lifestyle.help: Books, computers, sports equipment, internet and similar lifestyle expenses.

education.label: Education fees (RM)

controlTower.howDescription: What runs, in what order, which parts use AI, and what is switched on right now.
controlTower.loopIntro: Every cycle runs the same five steps. Only one of them involves AI, and none of them decides anything on its own.
controlTower.loopAlt: Five steps: checks run, findings are recorded, AI explains them in plain words, a person decides, and the result feeds back.
controlTower.step2Sub: with the figures that caused them
controlTower.step3Sub: AI writes it in plain words
controlTower.step4Sub: accept, fix, or approve what the AI proposes closing
controlTower.step5Sub: measures how well it is doing
controlTower.loopBack: What people decide is what tells us whether the checks are set right.
controlTower.agentsIntro: Read live from your own setup, not from a list someone wrote. If something says it is off, the reason is next to it.

agent.detectorsDoes: Looks at every employee in a finished payroll run and decides whether it is clear, needs a look, or must be blocked. No AI is involved and the answer never varies for the same figures.
agent.sweepDoes: Runs the checks every night at 02:30 so the queue is already filled when you open it, instead of waiting for someone to press a button.
agent.narratorDoes: Turns a finding into a sentence you can read. It can only use the figures already recorded — if it produces a number those figures do not support, the sentence is thrown away rather than shown.
agent.assistantDoes: Answers employees’ questions about their own records — leave, pay, and why their pay changed — so they do not have to ask a person.
agent.autonomyDoes: Clearing or changing anything without a person. Nothing in this system does this today.
agent.actionsDoes: Finds exceptions that were raised because something was missing from an employee record — and that record now has it. It proposes closing them; you approve, and each one is checked again as you do. It never changes an employee record.
agent.hypothesesDoes: Looks again at the people the fixed checks cleared, and compares each of them with their colleagues on the same payroll run. It can only ever ask for a second look — it can never block a run — and anything it suggests that we cannot re-derive from your own figures is thrown away before you see it.
agent.nudgeDoes: Notices whose record is missing something payroll needs, and tells the one person who can fix it — the employee for their own bank details, HR for everything only HR can key in. It sends nothing until you switch it on.
agent.payRuleDrafterDoes: Turns a sentence like “RM5 for every hour worked” into one of a fixed set of pay rules, which is then checked by the same code the payroll engine uses. It never saves anything — you review it and press save.
agent.reportDesignerDoes: Turns a description of a report into a draft layout, checked against the same rules the report builder enforces. It sees the shape of your data, never the data.
agent.reviewDrafterDoes: Drafts the wording of a manager’s performance review from what has already been recorded. The manager edits it and owns it; nothing is saved on their behalf.
agent.planDrafterDoes: Drafts a reply to an improvement request raised from inside the product. This is our own tooling rather than a feature of your plan.
agent.triageDoes: Reads each expense claim as it is filed and, if the description does not fit the rest of the claim, asks the person who filed it — before an approver spends time on it. It can only ever ask a question: it cannot refuse a claim, change one, or decide one.

why.moduleOff: Payroll is not part of your plan, so there is nothing to check.

why.sweepNever: Has never run. The queue will stay empty until it does.
why.narratorOn: A provider is set up and every finding has been explained.
why.narratorReady: A provider is set up. Explanations are written when you ask for them, on the exceptions screen.
why.noProvider: No AI provider is set up, so nothing can be explained. Everything else still works — you see the figures without the sentence.
why.assistantOn: You have access to the assistant.
why.assistantNoGrant: Not switched on for you. An administrator turns it on per person, under Administration → Users.
why.autonomyByDesign: Deliberately off. Nothing is cleared or changed without a person, and that will only change one action at a time, once we can show the system agrees with your people often enough to earn it.
why.actionsOn: Proposing on the Agent actions screen. Nothing is closed until you approve it.
why.hypothesesOn: Running every night on the people the fixed checks cleared. Anything it raises is for review only and never blocks a payroll run.
why.hypothesesOff: Not switched on. The fixed checks still run; this is the extra look that compares each person with their colleagues, and it stays off until you ask for it.
why.nudgeOn: Switched on. Reminders go out on the nightly run.
why.nudgeOff: Not switched on. Nobody is contacted automatically until you ask for it.
why.draftOnlyOn: A provider is set up. It drafts only when you ask, and nothing is saved until you say so.
why.planDrafterOff: Deliberately off. This is Stradaverse’s own tooling, not part of your plan.
why.triageOn: Reading new claims every night and asking the person who filed them. Nothing it asks can refuse or change a claim.
why.triageOff: Not switched on. Claims are read by people only, and nobody is asked anything automatically.

controlTower.domainsIntro: Payroll is the first area. The same machinery is built to cover the others, and they are listed here so you can see what is coming rather than assuming payroll is all there is.

domain.payrollDoes: Checks every finished payroll run for figures that look wrong, missing bank or tax details, and pay without attendance.
domain.readinessDoes: Would check every employee record all the time, not just at payroll, so a missing bank account is found and fixed long before it blocks anyone’s pay.
domain.onboardingDoes: Would check that a new joiner’s record is complete and correct before their first payroll, instead of finding out during it.
domain.complianceDoes: Would watch for changes to contribution rates and forms, and prepare the update for you to approve.

controlTower.promisesTitle: Two things this will not do
controlTower.promise1: AI never works out your pay.
controlTower.promise1Body: Every figure — salary, tax, contributions, overtime — is calculated by the payroll engine, the same way every time, and tested against known answers. AI is only ever used to describe a figure that has already been calculated. It cannot change one.
controlTower.promise2: AI never decides anything on its own.
controlTower.promise2Body: Whether something is cleared, flagged or blocked is decided by fixed rules before any AI is involved, and the explanation cannot change that decision. Nothing is cleared, paid or altered without a person.

readinessScreen.title: Record readiness
readinessScreen.description: Every active employee is either ready to be paid and filed for, or has something missing. Fix it here, once, instead of meeting it again every payroll.
readinessScreen.liveNote: Worked out fresh each time you open this page, so it is never out of date.
readinessScreen.allReady: All {n} active employees have everything needed to be paid and filed for. Nothing to fix.
readinessScreen.moreNotShown: Showing {shown} of {total}. Fix these and reload to see the rest.

gap.no_compensationFix: Set their salary on the employee record. Until then payroll has nothing to calculate for them.
gap.no_bank_accountFix: Add the bank account on the employee record. Only people paid by bank transfer are listed — anyone paid in cash or by cheque is not.
gap.no_identityFix: Add an IC or a passport number. Either one is enough; without one they cannot appear on any statutory submission.
gap.no_tax_numberFix: Add the LHDN tax number so their monthly tax deduction can be filed against it.
gap.no_epf_numberFix: Add the KWSP number so the contribution file can name them.
gap.no_socso_numberFix: Add the PERKESO number so the contribution file can name them.

actions.title: Agent actions
actions.description: Work the AI would like to take off your desk. Nothing here happens until you approve it, and you can see exactly why each one is being proposed.
actions.emptyBody: Every payroll exception still waiting on you has a real problem behind it. When somebody fixes the underlying record, the exception will appear here to be closed.
actions.staleNote: The other {stale} were left open. They were checked again as you approved, and no longer qualified — either the problem has come back, or somebody had already dealt with them.
actions.reversibleNote: This only records a decision about the exception. It changes no pay, no rate and no employee record, and checking the payroll run again replaces it.
actions.recheckNote: Each one is checked again the moment you press this. Anything that has gone wrong again since the page loaded is left open.
actions.overCap: One approval closes at most {cap}, and there are {total}. Approve these, then come back for the rest.

type.close_fixed_upstream: Close exceptions that are already fixed

error.unknown_type: That is not an action this system can take.

error.nothing_to_do: Nothing was selected, so nothing was closed.
error.failed: That could not be completed. Nothing was closed.

profileRequestSettings.title: Employee Change Requests
profileRequestSettings.description: Which fields of their own record an employee may ask to change, and who decides.
profileRequestSettings.readOnlyNotice: You can see this configuration but not change it — only a group administrator can.
profileRequestSettings.approverHelp: One person decides each request, and nobody can ever decide their own. Both choices are administrators because approving writes the master record, and only an administrator may write it — see the note below.

approverOptionHelp.admin: Including an administrator whose access covers one company. This is how the system behaves today if you change nothing.
approverOptionHelp.group_admin: A super administrator, or an HR administrator whose access covers the whole group. An administrator for a single company can no longer sign these off.

profileRequestSettings.singleLevelNote: A request is settled by one decision. There is no second level of approval, and a manager cannot be made the approver — approving writes the employee record itself, which only an administrator is permitted to do.
profileRequestSettings.unknownApprover: That is not one of the approver options.
profileRequestSettings.fieldsHeading: What an employee may ask to change
profileRequestSettings.fieldsHelp: Tick a field to let employees ask you to correct it. Unticked fields are simply not offered on their screen — there is no greyed-out box for them to wonder about.
profileRequestSettings.lockWithdrawsNotice: Switching a field off also refuses any request already waiting on it. The employee is told why, on their own screen. Nothing is applied to the record and nothing is deleted.
profileRequestSettings.withdrawnReason: This field is no longer open to change requests. Please contact HR if it still needs correcting.

refused.not_group_admin: Only a group administrator can change this.
refused.not_tenant_scoped: That setting is not yours to change.
refused.not_customer_visible: That setting is managed by Stradaverse.
